Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

 CLOSED SESSION REPORT

 City Attorney Marco Martinez reported City Council met in closed session and reported there were no reportable
 actions.

 CEREMONIAL

 1.  Recognition of City of Azusa Community Improvement Manager Rick McMinn, for receiving a Lifetime
 Achievement Award from the California Association of Code Enforcement Officers (CACEO).

 Economic & Community Development Director Jimenez presented City of Azusa Community Improvement
 Manager Rick McMinn with a Lifetime Achievement Award.

 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

 None.

 REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

 1.  **‘Pet of the Month’ Presentation by Los Angeles County Animal Care & Control.

 Baldwin Park Animal Control Officer provided the ‘Pet of the Month’ presentation regarding a one-year-old
 neutered Terrier named Roberto, who is available for adoption at Baldwin Park Animal Care Center, which is
 open Monday through Saturday from 11:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

 2.  **Economic Development Update.

 Economic & Community Development Director Jimenez provided a presentation regarding the Economic
 Development Year End Review and Jason Tolleson with Serrano Development Group provided an update on
 The Orchard project and responded to Council questions.

 3.  City Manager Communications.

 City Manager Gonzalez announced that the City Library Manager position has been reclassified to Lila, the new
 City Librarian.

 COUNCIL COMMENTS

 Mayor Pro-Tem Beckwith thanked Councilmember Mendez and all who put together the Santa Tour. Thanks to
 City staff for the excellent year and happy holidays. The City’s 125th Gala is scheduled for December 29, 2023,
 at the Linley Scott House.

 Councilmember Alvarez wished everyone a Merry Christmas and Happy New Year and urged those traveling to
 stay safe.

 Councilmember Avila Jr. congratulated Lila, Rick McMan, and all employees for a great year. December was a
 great month for community events. Great job to Mayor Gonzales and staff on the Azusa Resource Center (ARC).
 There have been six ribbon cuttings since September and thirty-four business licenses in the last quarter, great
 job by all those involved. Merry Christmas and Happy New Year to all.

 Councilmember Mendez expressed appreciation for the Christmas sweater contest and festive Council meeting,
 and for the City’s 4th Santa Tour. He thanked Chief Wenrick and the entire department for their efforts,
 congratulation to Lila for being selected for the City Librarian position. Merry Christmas and Happy New Year.

 Mayor Gonzales expressed appreciation to City staff for all their hard work. Thanks to Public Works staff for
 making the downtown area more festive by decorating the poles with Christmas lighting. He recommended

 toy drives.
